Its decodeframe.c line map (4704, 4484, 4489, 4398) matches the saved ASan trace; sample metadata names ed830191a9b18de28218786662c865ccec2c9bd0, a later still-vulnerable commit with shifted line numbers.

bug_description.original: Crash Type: Heap-use-after-free WRITE 2; Crash State: read_uncompressed_header / av1_decode_frame_headers_and_setup / aom_decode_frame_from_obus; Sanitizer: address (ASAN)
bug_description.normalized: In libaom's AV1 decoder, an earlier `RefCntBuffer` slot is released through `av1_release_frame_buffer()`, which makes its internal frame buffer reusable without clearing the slot's cached `YV12_BUFFER_CONFIG` plane pointers. A later `setup_buffer_pool()` call reuses that internal buffer for `cm->new_fb_idx`, and `av1_get_frame_buffer()` frees the old `int_fb[i].data`, leaving the released slot's wrapper dangling. When a later changed sequence header followed by a key frame calls `reset_frame_buffers()`, the reset loop unconditionally repaints every `frame_bufs[i].buf` with `set_planes_to_neutral_grey()`, including the stale released slot, causing a heap-use-after-free WRITE in the high-bitdepth neutral-grey fill.

source.description: On the later free-causing frame, this call consumes attacker-controlled frame-size-related bits from the bit buffer and materializes the geometry used to size the current frame buffer.
source.value_from: The staged 221-byte witness is split by common/ivfdec.c into three 51-byte compressed AV1 frame payloads: the little-endian size word 0x33 appears at offsets 0x20, 0x5d, and 0x9a in the PoC bytes. Those payload bytes are later read through the aom_read_bit_buffer `rb` inside read_uncompressed_header().
source.note: ASan's free stack shows this call reaching setup_buffer_pool() and av1_get_frame_buffer(), where the heap region later written through the stale frame_bufs slot is freed.

sink.description: Writes a 16-bit neutral-grey value through `buf->buffers[plane]` from a stale `YV12_BUFFER_CONFIG` wrapper whose backing heap storage was freed earlier.
sink.note: This is the ASan crash site: heap-use-after-free WRITE of size 2 in the high-bitdepth branch of set_planes_to_neutral_grey().

root_cause.description: reset_frame_buffers() repaints every `frame_bufs[i].buf` without restricting the repaint to the current live buffer or checking that the slot still has valid backing storage, so released stale wrappers are dereferenced.
root_cause.note: Inside `reset_frame_buffers()`, `seq_params` comes from `&cm->seq_params`, so the later stored sequence-header state drives the repaint. In the vulnerable loop, lines 4391-4393 release non-current `raw_frame_buffer` ownership but do not clear `frame_bufs[i].buf`; the immediately following repaint still dereferences that wrapper. The fix moves the repaint into the `i == cm->new_fb_idx` case and adds a `buffer_alloc_sz >= frame_size` guard.

tainted_value_origin.description: The fuzzer harness interprets the witness after its fixed 32-byte prefix as three IVF-style frame records; ivf_read_frame() reads three frame sizes of 51 bytes and then passes those 51-byte payloads to the AV1 decoder.

parser_admitted.description: The later sequence header OBU is accepted and stored, so subsequent frame-header parsing in read_uncompressed_header() evaluates the changed-sequence keyframe reset path.

coarse_trace.summary: Splits the staged witness into three 51-byte compressed AV1 frame payloads and feeds them to the decoder.
An earlier frame retires a RefCntBuffer slot; the internal release callback marks its raw frame buffer reusable but leaves the slot's cached YV12 plane pointers intact, creating a stale wrapper.

A later frame parses attacker-controlled geometry and resizes the current slot; av1_get_frame_buffer() reuses the released internal buffer and frees its old backing allocation, turning the stale wrapper's plane pointers into dangling pointers.

A later sequence header OBU parses new structural and color parameters, stores them into `cm->seq_params`, differs from the prior stored header, and sets `sequence_header_changed` while selecting the high-bitdepth path.
The triggering frame header parses KEY_FRAME, so the changed-sequence path calls reset_frame_buffers().

The reset loop uses the stored later `cm->seq_params` and repaints every frame_bufs[i].buf with `set_planes_to_neutral_grey()`, including the stale released slot whose plane pointers still alias the freed heap region, and the high-bitdepth store writes into freed memory.

fine_trace.note: Earlier in the same witness, some `RefCntBuffer` reaches `ref_count == 0`, so `decrease_ref_count()` releases its `raw_frame_buffer`. The precise caller that dropped the final reference is not preserved in Stage 01 artifacts, but `av1_get_frame_buffer()` can only later reuse an internal buffer after this release path runs.

In the staged internal-buffer build, `init_buffer_callbacks()` installs `av1_release_frame_buffer` as `release_fb_cb`. This callback marks the internal buffer reusable and clears only `fb->priv`; it does not clear `fb->data` or the slot's cached `YV12_BUFFER_CONFIG` plane pointers, so `frame_bufs[idx].buf.buffers[plane]` still alias that internal allocation after release.

On the later free-causing frame, this call consumes size-related bits from `rb` and the current sequence parameters, updates the frame geometry, and reaches `setup_buffer_pool()`. That geometry determines the reallocation request that reuses an internal buffer.

setup_buffer_pool() asks `aom_realloc_frame_buffer()` to size only the current `cm->new_fb_idx` slot for the parsed geometry and current color state. Other `frame_bufs[*].buf` wrappers are not rewritten here, so a slot made stale at step 2 keeps its cached `buffers[plane]` pointers.

When the reusable internal buffer chosen for the current slot is too small, `av1_get_frame_buffer()` frees its old `int_fb[i].data` before allocating a larger block. ASan's free stack points here. Because step 2 left another `frame_bufs[idx].buf.buffers[plane]` wrapper aliased to this same internal buffer, those plane pointers become dangling when the old data is freed.
Later in the same witness, a new sequence-header OBU is parsed into `seq_params`, materializing the later sequence's structural parameters from attacker-controlled bits.
The later sequence header's color config sets the current bit depth and `use_highbitdepth`. In the staged crash, this selects the 16-bit neutral-grey write path used at the sink.
Because the newly parsed `seq_params` is not bytewise consistent with the previously stored `cm->seq_params`, the decoder marks that the sequence header changed.

The decoder copies the newly parsed local sequence header into persistent decoder state. This write carries the later sequence's `bit_depth` and `use_highbitdepth` into `cm->seq_params`, which `reset_frame_buffers()` and `set_planes_to_neutral_grey()` read on the crash path.

For the later frame-header OBU, `aom_decode_frame_from_obus()` initializes a fresh local `rb` over that OBU's payload bytes. This `rb` is distinct from the earlier sequence-header OBU's `rb` because the loop declares a new `struct aom_read_bit_buffer rb` at line 663 and reinitializes it for each OBU.
Using the later frame-header `rb` from step 10, `read_uncompressed_header()` reads `KEY_FRAME`, satisfying the branch that allows a changed sequence header to reset all frame buffers.
With `pbi->sequence_header_changed` set and `cm->frame_type == KEY_FRAME`, `read_uncompressed_header()` calls `reset_frame_buffers()` for the new sequence.

Inside `reset_frame_buffers()`, `seq_params` points at `cm->seq_params`, i.e. the global copy from step 9. The loop still unconditionally calls `set_planes_to_neutral_grey()` on every slot's `YV12_BUFFER_CONFIG`, not just `cm->new_fb_idx`, and does not verify that the wrapper still has live backing storage. A slot whose plane pointers were left stale at step 2 and made dangling at step 5 is therefore passed into the fill routine with the updated later-sequence parameters. The fix moves this repaint to the current buffer only and adds a `buffer_alloc_sz >= frame_size` guard.

Using the `seq_params` passed from step 13, the function takes the high-bitdepth branch, converts `buf->buffers[plane]` to `uint16_t *base`, and writes `val` through the dangling plane pointer in that stale buffer wrapper. ASan reports a heap-use-after-free WRITE of size 2 here.

poc.trigger: The staged 221-byte witness is interpreted by av1_dec_fuzzer as three 51-byte frame payloads after a 32-byte prefix. After an earlier frame slot has been released but its wrapper retained, a later frame causes `av1_get_frame_buffer()` to free that slot's old internal backing storage, and a later inconsistent sequence header plus key frame makes `reset_frame_buffers()` repaint the stale slot, reaching the ASan WRITE-2 crash at `av1/decoder/decodeframe.c:99`.

format.name: av1_dec_fuzzer staged multi-frame AV1 stream
format.contract: Exactly the witnessed three-frame shape: after the 32-byte prefix, each frame record has little-endian length 0x33. Earlier payload bytes must drive the decoder to release a frame-buffer slot while leaving its `frame_bufs[i].buf` wrapper intact, then later `setup_frame_size()->setup_buffer_pool()->av1_get_frame_buffer()` must reuse that internal buffer and free its old `int_fb[i].data`; a later sequence header must differ from the stored header so `pbi->sequence_header_changed` becomes 1; the following frame header must parse as KEY_FRAME; and that later sequence header must select the high-bitdepth neutral-grey path. This is the verified trigger semantics for the staged witness, not a claim about all AV1 streams with changed sequence headers.
